body.p: I. Introduction

The undersigned thanks Examiner Yankey for review and consideration of the present Application. In response to the Office Action of February 15, 2024 ("Office Action"), the undersigned submits the present amendment and remarks ("Response").

Upon entry of the present amendment, claims 24-40 will be pending in this application. Claim 24 has been amended, and claims 1-23 and 41 have been cancelled. No new matter is added. Based on the following remarks, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims.
AFCP 2.0 Request:

Furthermore, it is respectfully submitted that this Amendment should be considered and entered under the Patent Office's "After Final Consideration Pilot Program 2.0" (AFCP 2.0) because the contents of the response herein may lead to allowance of the application with only limited further search and/or consideration. Applicant's representative is willing and available to participate in any interview requested by the examiner concerning the present response. II. Claim Reijections under 35 U.S.C. " 102 & 103

Claims 38-40 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent Publication No. 2018/0281963 Al to Dowty et al. ("Dowty"). Claims 24-36 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dowty in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2013/0248655 Al to Kroll et al. ("Kroll"). Claim 37 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dowty in view of Kroll as applied to claim 24 above in view of U.S. Patent No. 5,024,398 to Riedinger et al. ("Riedinger"). Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration as explained below.
A. Claims 24-37

Applicant submits that claim 24 is allowable at least because Dowty and Kroll fail to teach or suggest at least "the front side of the storage unit provides access from the aircraft passenger seat unit to the holders of the storage unit" (emphasis added) as recited in claim 24.

The Office Action asserts that Dowty an aircraft seat unit with a seat, a privacy shell with a primary opening (formed by 2602 and 2609), a storage unit (2504) having a back side and a front side as marked below, and a door (2609 and 2502). Office Action pages 6-7.

However, as self-evident by the express teachings of Dowty as well as the interpretation offered by the Office Action, the front side of the alleged storage unit 2504 is outward-facing and is only accessible from the aisle, or outside the aircraft seat unit. See, e.g., FIG. 25A below and paragraphs [0134] and [0135] ("the forward cabin monument 2604 includes aisle-side doors or openings") (emphasis added). Nowhere does Dowty teach or suggest "the front side of the storage unit provides access from the aircraft passenger seat unit to the holders of the storage unit" (emphasis added) as recited in claim 24. Moreover, based on the teachings of Dowty, the skilled person would not somehow modify the aisle-side opening. For example per the teachings of Dowty, the forward cabin monument can include "galley compartments" and "electronics compartments" (paragraph [0003]), which would be accessible by aircraft staff, and therefore be

accessed from the aisle (rather than from inside a passenger seat unit). There is no suggestion in Dowty that an entrance to a forward cabin monument could be moved, or that it would be desirable to do so.

For at least this reason, Dowty fails to teach or suggest "the front side of the storage unit provides access from the aircraft passenger seat unit to the holders of the storage unit" as recited in claim 24. Kroll does not cure this deficiency, nor was it cited for such a purpose.

For at least these reasons, claim 24 is allowable. Claims 25-37 are allowable at least because they depend from claim 24 and may be allowable for additional reasons. Withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.
B. Claims 38-40

Applicant submits that claim 38 is allowable at least because Dowty fails to teach or suggest at least because Dowty fails to teach or suggest at least a "privacy shell having a primary opening defining a first and second edge to allow entry to and exit from the seat unit" and "a

door, movable between a first position in which the door at least partially blocks off the primary opening, and a second position, in which the door provides at least partial access to the primary opening, wherein the door is arranged to move between the first and second positions in a direction offset by an angle from the first edge of the primary opening of the privacy shell" where "the first edge is adjacent to the door when the door is in the second position" and "the door is arranged to slide between the first position and the second position in a direction along a length of the door" as recited in claim 38.

Referring to the annotated figure below from the Office Action, the Office Action asserts that Dowty discloses a seat, a privacy shell (2504, 2506, 2508, 2510) with first and second edges, and a door (2502 and 2609). Office Action pages 3-4. In particular, the Office Action asserts that "left and right sides of door [2502 and 2609] define[e] a first and second edge. Office Action page 3. Applicant respectfully disagrees with such an interpretation.

Applicant initially notes that the claim requires that the privacy shell include the edges defining the opening, not the door as alleged by the Office Action. A door does not define an opening, nor would the skilled person in the art understand a door to define an opening. The only
edges of Dowty that may define an opening are the aft edge of the forward cabin monument (2604) and the aisle-side privacy panel.

Moreover, while the Office Action has interpreted the door required by the claim to include both the door assembly 2602 and the filler door 2609, FIG. 26E of Dowty discloses a passenger suite comprising two doors, each slidable in a direction along the length of the particular door between a first position and a second position in which the door is adjacent to the first edge of the primary opening. The doors in FIG. 26E do not move together or constitute a single door.

Once the edges defining an opening as well as the door are properly considered, neither the door assembly 2602 nor the filler door 2609 are disclosed to slide in a direction offset from the first edge (the aisle side privacy panel 2508 and the aft edge of the forward cabin monument 2604 respectively), wherein the first edge is the edge adjacent to the door when the door is in the second position.

In other words, claim 38 requires that the edge of the opening that the door is adjacent to when in the access providing position is the edge to which the door is offset from when it slides. Instead, in Dowty, the door assembly 2602 slides along (i.e. in a direction aligned with) the side privacy panel 2508 (unchanged from FIG. 25, see paragraph [0129]). Similarly, the filler door 2609 slides along (i.e. in a direction aligned with) the aisle side edge 2606 of the forward cabin monument (see paragraph [0134]). Neither door slides in a direction that is offset from the edge that they are adjacent to when in the second position (i.e. the access providing position).

For at least this reason, Dowty fails to teach all elements of claim 38 and thus fails to anticipate claim 38, and claim 38 is allowable over Dowty. Claims 39 and 40 are allowable because they depend from claim 38 and may be allowable for additional reasons. Withdrawal fo the rejection is respectfully requested.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant believes all claims now pending in this application are in condition for allowance. The issuance of a formal Notice of Allowance at an early date is respectfully requested.
